# Tile-based Rasterization with Radix Sort

Also called: Tiled 2D Gaussian Splatting Rasterization with Global Radix Sort

## Overview
Tile-based Rasterization with Radix Sort is a GPU-parallel rasterization method for 3D Gaussian Splatting that divides the image into tiles to manage memory and processing load, assigning Gaussians to tiles based on their projected 2D splats [Tiled 2D Gaussian Splatting Rasterization](2061-tiled-2d-gaussian-splatting-rasterization.md). It solves the performance bottleneck of per-pixel sorting by using a single global radix sort to achieve per-tile depth ordering, enabling real-time performance for millions of splats [Tile-based Rasteriser](2846-tile-based-rasteriser.md). Unlike sibling methods that may perform redundant depth sorting or evaluate splats against irrelevant pixels, this method ensures that each tile is processed by one GPU thread block walking a single sorted list [Tile-based Rasteriser](2846-tile-based-rasteriser.md).

## Shared principles
The method operates on a list of $N$ projected 2D Gaussian splats, each defined by center $(x_i, y_i)$, 2D covariance matrix $\Sigma'_i$, color $c_i$, opacity $\alpha_i$, and depth $Z_c$ [Tile-based Rasteriser](2846-tile-based-rasteriser.md). The image is divided into a grid of tiles with dimensions $T_w \times T_h$ (typically $16 \times 16$ pixels) [Tile-based Rasteriser](2846-tile-based-rasteriser.md).

The core mechanism involves three phases:

1. **Tile Assignment:** Each Gaussian is assigned to every tile its projected 2D splat touches. If a splat straddles tile boundaries, it is duplicated into each relevant tile [Tile-based Rasteriser](2846-tile-based-rasteriser.md). This creates one work item per (Gaussian, tile) pair [Tile-based Rasteriser](2846-tile-based-rasteriser.md).
2. **Key Packing:** For each (splat, tile) pair, a 64-bit integer sort key is constructed. The tile ID is packed into the high bits, and the splat's depth $Z_c$ is packed into the low bits [Tile-based Rasteriser](2846-tile-based-rasteriser.md). Specifically, the key is formed as:
   $$ \text{key} = (\text{tile\_id} \ll 32) \mid (\text{uint32\_t})Z_c $$
   where `tile_id` is the 1D tile index ($y \times \text{grid\_width} + x$) and $Z_c$ is cast to a 32-bit unsigned integer [Tile-based Rasteriser](2846-tile-based-rasteriser.md).
3. **Global Radix Sort:** A single GPU radix sort is performed over all (splat, tile) pairs [Tile-based Rasteriser](2846-tile-based-rasteriser.md). This simultaneously bins splats by tile ID (ensuring contiguity) and sorts them by depth within each tile [Tile-based Rasteriser](2846-tile-based-rasteriser.md).

After sorting, each tile is processed by one GPU thread block that walks the sorted list [Tile-based Rasteriser](2846-tile-based-rasteriser.md). For each pixel in a tile, front-to-back compositing is performed using the tile's sorted list of splats, evaluating per-pixel alpha $\alpha_i(\mathbf{x})$ and breaking early when transmittance $T < \epsilon$ [Tile-based Rasteriser](2846-tile-based-rasteriser.md). The same sorted lists are reused for backpropagation, allowing gradients to flow to position, shape, opacity, and color without additional sorting [Tile-based Rasteriser](2846-tile-based-rasteriser.md).

## Subtopics

### [Tile-Based Culling](2819-tile-based-culling.md)
Computes a precise mapping between 3D Gaussians and image tiles to eliminate irrelevant tiles during rasterization. It sets itself apart from the parent method by iteratively examining candidate tiles to verify actual overlap rather than assigning a Gaussian to every tile its projected splat touches, reducing radix sort workload. Choose it when conservative bounding boxes cause excessive overdraw.

### [Tile-based Rasteriser](2846-tile-based-rasteriser.md)
A GPU-optimized rendering component that sorts projected 2D Gaussian splats once per frame to serve both forward rendering and backpropagation. It sets itself apart from per-pixel sorting methods by dividing the image into tiles and using a single global radix sort to achieve per-tile depth ordering. Choose it for real-time performance with millions of splats.

### [Gaussian Rasterization Key Generation](5133-gaussian-rasterization-key-generation.md)
Generates the key-value pairs required for tile-based depth sorting in 3D Gaussian Splatting. It sets itself apart from filtering methods by explicitly generating the full set of overlaps for sorting rather than just discarding them. Choose it as the direct input stage for the global radix sort.

### [FlashGS](7331-flashgs.md)
A multi-GPU rendering and training method for 3D Gaussian Splatting that accelerates the forward pass by partitioning the screen into finer tiles and scheduling them across a multi-GPU pipeline. It sets itself apart from single-GPU rasterizers by distributing the tile workload to enable scalability for large scenes. Choose it for multi-GPU setups requiring high throughput.

### [Tile-based Depth Sorting](8038-tile-based-depth-sorting.md)
A rasterization strategy designed to mitigate "popping" artifacts in surface-based volumetric representations where Gaussian distributions are concentrated on surfaces. It sets itself apart from standard 3D Gaussian Splatting by enforcing strict consistency between forward rendering and backward gradient computation traversal orders. Choose it when viewpoint rotation causes blending order artifacts.

### [Opacity-Thresholded Tile Intersection Filtering](2109-opacity-thresholded-tile-intersection-filtering.md)
Filters out Gaussians during the tile intersection phase if their opacity falls below a specified alpha-threshold, treating their axis-aligned bounding box as effectively empty. It sets itself apart from precise culling methods by using a simple threshold check rather than iterative tile examination. Choose it to reduce the number of Gaussians requiring sorting and shading.

### [Tile Range Identification](5135-tile-range-identification.md)
Determines the contiguous start and end indices of each tile's Gaussian splats within a globally sorted list. It sets itself apart from culling methods by operating on the post-sort data structure to define access bounds rather than filtering splats. Choose it to map the flat, sorted array back to per-tile ranges for efficient iteration.

## Background
The method builds on [Tiled 2D Gaussian Splatting Rasterization](2061-tiled-2d-gaussian-splatting-rasterization.md). The specific optimizations regarding opacity-thresholded filtering and performance gains are detailed in [Tile-Based Culling](2819-tile-based-culling.md). The implementation details and unofficial variations are documented in [Tile Range Identification](5135-tile-range-identification.md).
